resources.string: Sends Back, so one push of Back closes the keyboard and goes back. While the Sym panel is open, in the Smart Launcher search field and for a moment after you push Back, TitanKeys sees the keys you push. It can\'t read your screen, and it doesn\'t keep or send anything.
Copy text, and it shows here for an hour.
To pin a clip, push Enter, then a key under the clip.
Push a key under a clip to pin or unpin it
Push Backspace or Clear again to clear all but pinned

Clipboard. The texts that you copied in the last hour, and the ones you pinned. Push a key under a clip to paste it. Swipe up or down to see more, and left or right for Pinned. Enter pins, Backspace clears, and Alt goes back.
Older clips: push Sym, then A
To use names from your contacts, allow Contacts for TitanKeys on this page.
TitanKeys can use Android\'s Accessibility service to make Back and a few keys work better. It\'s optional.
Back: when you push Back, TitanKeys sends it on for you, so one push closes the keyboard and goes back in the app.
Keys: at these times only, it sees which keys you push before the app does:
while the Sym panel is open, so Enter and Backspace turn its pages instead of reaching the app;
in the Smart Launcher search field, so holding a key for a symbol and pushing Shift or Alt twice work there;
for a moment after you push Back, so your next push of Back reaches the app.
It can\'t read your screen or the text in your apps.
It doesn\'t keep or send the keys it sees. They\'re used on your phone straight away, then forgotten.
If you say no: TitanKeys still types and swipes. Back may take two pushes, and those keys work as they would without TitanKeys. You can turn it on later in Settings > Setup.
